concepts.label: Agriculture
concepts.learning_takeaway: How growing crops and raising animals supply food and materials.
concepts.card: Agriculture combines cultivating soil, growing crops and raising animals to supply food and other materials. Its products extend beyond meals: cotton and wool become textiles, while livestock can also supply leather. Farming connects living organisms with the materials people use.
concepts.original_description: practice of cultivating plants and raising animals to produce food, fiber, fuel, and other products; one of humanity's oldest and most widespread activities, forming the foundation of most human civilizations

evidence.locator: Opening explanation; lines 39-40
evidence.note: Cultivation and livestock provide food and material products.

imported_records.description: practice of cultivating plants and raising animals to produce food, fiber, fuel, and other products; one of humanity's oldest and most widespread activities, forming the foundation of most human civilizations

concepts.label: Epidemiology
concepts.learning_takeaway: How population patterns and causes of health events inform disease control.
concepts.card: Epidemiology studies how health events are distributed through populations and what influences them. Comparing patterns across people, places and times helps investigate causes and guide public-health action. The field concerns population health broadly, rather than only treating one person's illness.
concepts.original_description: study of the patterns, causes, and effects of health and disease conditions

evidence.locator: Definition and distribution; lines 11-22, 41-46
evidence.note: Population distribution and determinants guide public-health action.

imported_records.description: study of the patterns, causes, and effects of health and disease conditions

concepts.label: Mathematics
concepts.learning_takeaway: Abstract structures can become tools for quantitative practical problems.
concepts.card: Mathematics studies idealized objects such as numbers and shapes, developing tools for reasoning about them. Some tools address abstract questions; others help solve practical quantitative problems. The same field can explore a structure for its own sake and use it elsewhere.

evidence.locator: Opening definition; line 13
evidence.note: Abstract objects and practical quantitative tools.

concepts.label: Sewing
concepts.learning_takeaway: How seams and stitch choices turn fabric pieces into a usable object.
concepts.card: Sewing joins fabric pieces with stitches to construct an object. A patchwork pillow illustrates the process: separate squares become a larger panel, then a cover. Stitch choices serve different purposes, including permanent joining and temporary holding during construction.
concepts.original_description: Constructing and altering items through stitched fabric pieces.

evidence.locator: Pillow construction; basting; lines 114-130, 165-167
evidence.note: Pillow construction joins pieces and uses temporary basting.

imported_records.description: Constructing and altering items through stitched fabric pieces.

concepts.label: Physics
concepts.learning_takeaway: How a few physical principles connect particles, everyday devices and motion.
concepts.card: Physics studies energy, matter, space and time and the interactions among them. Its principles connect phenomena at very different scales, from particles to everyday devices. Understanding a device's operation can therefore involve the same underlying physical rules used to explain motion elsewhere.
concepts.original_description: Studying matter, energy and their fundamental interactions.

evidence.locator: Science and the Realm of Physics; lines 37-40
evidence.note: Fundamental interactions connect scales and everyday technologies.

imported_records.description: Studying matter, energy and their fundamental interactions.

concepts.label: Chemistry
concepts.learning_takeaway: How composition and interactions of matter connect cooking, materials and medicine.
concepts.card: Chemistry investigates what matter contains, how it behaves, and how substances interact. These questions connect familiar activities such as cooking with the development of medicines and materials. Changes in everyday substances become examples of the same broader study of matter.
concepts.original_description: Studying substances, their properties and their transformations.

evidence.locator: Chemistry: The Central Science; lines 44-54
evidence.note: Matter's composition, properties and interactions connect everyday applications.

imported_records.description: Studying substances, their properties and their transformations.

concepts.label: Geology
concepts.learning_takeaway: How present rocks and landscapes preserve evidence of Earth's long history.
concepts.card: Geology studies Earth's materials, water and processes, including changes that unfold over immense spans of time. Rocks and landscapes preserve evidence of earlier conditions. Reading that evidence helps connect the present Earth with a history much longer than direct human observation.
concepts.original_description: Investigating Earth's materials, structures and history.

evidence.locator: Opening definition and deep time; lines 338-340
evidence.note: Earth materials and processes are interpreted across deep time.

imported_records.description: Investigating Earth's materials, structures and history.

concepts.label: Biology
concepts.learning_takeaway: How the study of life connects cells, organisms and ecosystems.
concepts.card: Biology studies life, from the workings of cells to organisms and the ecosystems they inhabit. Looking across these scales connects small structures with larger living systems: a question about an organism can also involve its cells and environment.
concepts.original_description: Studying living organisms and their interactions.

evidence.locator: What is biology?; Natural Sciences; lines 33-49
evidence.note: Life studied across cells, organisms and ecosystems.

imported_records.description: Studying living organisms and their interactions.

concepts.label: 101955 Bennu
concepts.learning_takeaway: An asteroid assembled from old rocky debris can be sampled to investigate Solar-System history.
concepts.card: 101955 Bennu is a rubble-pile asteroid assembled from older rocky debris. The age of its constituent rocks differs from the age of the assembled object. NASA's OSIRIS-REx collected a sample in 2020 and returned it in 2023, enabling direct investigation.

evidence.locator: Rubble-pile structure and sample collection; lines 239-252
evidence.note: Assembled debris structure and dated OSIRIS-REx sample return.

relations.note: NASA explicitly identifies Bennu as an asteroid.

concepts.label: Apoplast
concepts.learning_takeaway: Water can travel through connected cell-wall and extracellular spaces.
concepts.card: The apoplast is the connected space of plant cell walls and extracellular regions. Water can move through this route outside the cytoplasm. In roots, the Casparian strip interrupts it, requiring water to cross a cell membrane.

evidence.locator: The significance of the casparian strip; lines 234-242
evidence.note: Wall route interrupted by the Casparian barrier.

relations.note: Transport premises support editorial plant-physiology placement.

concepts.label: Bankfull discharge
concepts.learning_takeaway: Field channel indicators and hydraulic models can be combined to estimate flow at bankfull stage.
concepts.card: Bankfull discharge is river flow associated with the natural bankfull stage. Field indicators help identify that water level, while channel cross sections and hydraulic estimates help check the corresponding flow. Regional recurrence patterns can assist interpretation, but are not a universal definition.

evidence.locator: Abstract; line 7
evidence.note: Natural bankfull stage defines the flow under study.

evidence.locator: Bankfull field indicators and cross-section checks; PDF page 15 (zero-based 14), lines 414-433
evidence.note: Field indicators and hydraulic checks estimate flow; recurrence is regional.

relations.note: Article explicitly studies river discharge at bankfull stage.

concepts.label: Basting in sewing
concepts.learning_takeaway: Long temporary stitches hold fabric together before permanent construction.
concepts.card: Basting in sewing uses long temporary stitches to hold fabric in position during construction. In a pillow project, basting secures a prepared piece before later stitching. Its purpose is temporary placement, so a basting line serves a different role from the final seam.

evidence.locator: Pillow construction; basting; lines 114-130, 165-167
evidence.note: Long temporary stitches hold prepared pillow fabric.

relations.note: Source explicitly uses the stitch in sewing.

concepts.label: Bayes factor
concepts.learning_takeaway: A marginal-likelihood ratio transforms prior model odds into posterior odds.
concepts.card: A Bayes factor compares two models through the ratio of their marginal likelihoods for observed data. Multiplying prior model odds by this ratio gives posterior odds. The evidence comparison therefore depends on the specified models and their parameter priors.

evidence.locator: Definition and odds identities; lines 7-17
evidence.note: Marginal-likelihood ratio updates model odds.

evidence.locator: Definition and marginalization identity; lines 7-8
evidence.note: Marginalization includes the specified model and its parameter prior.

relations.note: Definition explicitly belongs to Bayesian model selection.

concepts.label: Blood Falls
concepts.learning_takeaway: Iron-rich brine can flow from within a cold glacier and turn red when exposed to air.
concepts.card: Blood Falls is an iron-rich brine outflow from Antarctica's Taylor Glacier. The liquid turns red when its iron contacts air. Radar traced brine pathways within the cold glacier; dissolved salts lower the freezing point, helping explain liquid water inside such icy surroundings.

evidence.locator: Brine pathway and iron-rich outflow; lines 18-27
evidence.note: Iron-rich outflow and radar-mapped saline liquid explain the phenomenon.

relations.note: Source explicitly locates the brine system within a glacier.

concepts.label: Case hardening in food drying
concepts.learning_takeaway: An apparently dry surface can hide moisture retained inside a food piece.
concepts.card: Case hardening in food drying happens when excessive heat dries or cooks the outside before the interior dries. The surface can look dry while moisture remains inside. This hidden moisture can permit spoilage, showing why appearance alone does not describe the whole piece.

evidence.locator: Oven drying; lines 267-269
evidence.note: High heat hardens the surface and leaves a moist interior.

relations.note: Source explicitly describes a failure during food drying.

concepts.label: Casparian strip
concepts.learning_takeaway: A hydrophobic band interrupts movement through cell walls and forces membrane crossing.
concepts.card: The Casparian strip is a water-repelling band in root endodermal cell walls. It blocks continued movement along the apoplast, so water must cross a cell membrane before proceeding inward. A structural barrier thereby changes the available transport route.

evidence.locator: The significance of the casparian strip; lines 234-242
evidence.note: Endodermal wall barrier forces membrane crossing.

relations.note: Source identifies this band in root anatomy.

concepts.label: Coherent dedispersion
concepts.learning_takeaway: Deconvolve dispersion from recorded voltage data to recover a smeared radio pulse.
concepts.card: Coherent dedispersion corrects a pulsar's dispersed radio signal by deconvolving the interstellar medium's transfer function from recorded voltage data. With known dispersion and suitably sampled baseband data, it can remove dispersion's smearing, preserving sharp pulse structure for high-precision timing.

evidence.locator: Interstellar dispersion and coherent dedispersion; lines 250-255
evidence.note: Known dispersion and Nyquist-sampled voltages permit deconvolution.

relations.note: Signal-correction premises support an editorial radio-astronomy application.
Source explicitly applies the technique to pulsar timing.

concepts.label: Critical micelle concentration
concepts.learning_takeaway: A concentration threshold changes how added surfactant partitions into micelles.
concepts.card: At a surfactant's critical micelle concentration, molecules begin forming micellar aggregates in solution. Above this threshold, added surfactant mainly enters micelles while the monomer concentration stays approximately constant. The threshold is specified for particular conditions, including temperature and pressure.

evidence.locator: Characteristic concentration and monomer/micelle partition; lines 196-206
evidence.note: Threshold changes monomer versus micelle partitioning.

relations.note: Source explicitly defines a surfactant concentration threshold.

concepts.label: Cryosuction
concepts.learning_takeaway: Growing ice draws in liquid water that freezes, allowing a segregated layer to enlarge.
concepts.card: Cryosuction draws liquid water toward growing ice in freezing ground. As the incoming water freezes, it enlarges a segregated ice layer, which can attract still more water. This supplies ice growth beyond the water initially present at that location.

evidence.locator: Density of frozen water and cryosuction; lines 89-94
evidence.note: Growing ice attracts and freezes further water.

relations.note: Soil-water and ice-growth premises support editorial soil-physics placement.

concepts.label: Degrees Brix
concepts.learning_takeaway: A sucrose-calibrated scale helps compare soluble solids in fruit juice.
concepts.card: One degree Brix corresponds to one gram of sucrose per 100 grams of a sucrose-and-water solution. In fruit juice, a refractometer reports soluble solids on this scale, so the reading need not isolate sucrose from other dissolved substances.

evidence.locator: Table 4, definitions of sample parameters; line 1242
evidence.note: Sucrose scale measures fruit-juice soluble solids by refractometer.

relations.note: Refractometer use supports an editorial refractive-index application.

concepts.label: Deprescribing
concepts.learning_takeaway: Supervised medication reduction requires reviewing benefit, risk and subsequent symptoms.
concepts.card: Deprescribing is supervised medication discontinuation or dose reduction after reviewing appropriateness, benefits and risks with the patient. It requires continued monitoring: withdrawal symptoms or recurrence of the original problem can lead to dose adjustment or restarting. Reducing medication is an ongoing clinical decision.

evidence.locator: Definition and steps; lines 132-142; ongoing monitoring; line 169
evidence.note: Supervised shared decisions require monitoring for withdrawal or recurrence.

relations.note: Clinical medication-management premises support an editorial medicine application.

concepts.label: Desargues' theorem
concepts.learning_takeaway: Triangles sharing a center of perspectivity produce collinear intersections of corresponding sides.
concepts.card: In classical projective geometry, two triangles are perspective from a point when lines joining corresponding vertices meet there. Desargues' theorem links this to a line: the intersections of corresponding sides are collinear, connecting two different kinds of geometric alignment.

evidence.locator: Theorem statement; lines 16-19
evidence.note: Point perspectivity implies line perspectivity.

relations.note: Projective incidence premises support editorial projective-geometry placement.

concepts.label: Design ease
concepts.learning_takeaway: Extra room beyond wearing ease shapes a garment's outline and fullness.
concepts.card: Design ease is additional garment fullness chosen for style, beyond the room needed for comfortable wear. This extra allowance shapes the garment's outline; a pattern can combine comfort room with deliberately chosen styling.

evidence.locator: Wearing versus design ease; fabric edges; lines 84, 154, 178
evidence.note: Additional pattern fullness serves garment style.

relations.note: Guide explicitly defines a sewing-pattern styling component.

concepts.label: Dispersion measure
concepts.learning_takeaway: Radio pulse delays encode an integrated column of electrons along the line of sight.
concepts.card: Dispersion measure sums the free-electron density along a radio signal's path. For pulsars, this electron column determines frequency-dependent arrival delays: lower-frequency waves arrive later. It characterizes the intervening sightline, rather than being an intrinsic property of the pulsar.

evidence.locator: Section 6.2 Pulsars and the Interstellar Medium; equations 6.43–6.46 and following text; lines 241-255
evidence.note: Integrated electron column controls frequency-dependent propagation delay.

relations.note: Radio-propagation premises support editorial radio-astronomy placement.
Pulsar signals measure the intervening electron column.

concepts.label: Dryeration
concepts.learning_takeaway: Corn's retained heat supports extra drying after a resting period and slow cooling.
concepts.card: Dryeration separates corn drying from final cooling. Hot corn rests in a cooling bin before air is introduced; retained heat helps remove additional moisture during cooling. Using that remaining heat makes the cooling stage part of drying rather than only temperature reduction.

evidence.locator: Increased capacity and efficiency; Process; lines 263-290
evidence.note: Tempering and slow cooling use retained corn heat for drying.

relations.note: Guide explicitly identifies a corn-drying method.

concepts.label: Elysia chlorotica
concepts.learning_takeaway: This sea slug stabilizes ingested plastids during an early developmental feeding period.
concepts.card: Elysia chlorotica is a sea slug that retains chloroplasts from Vaucheria litorea. In a laboratory study, juveniles fed for seven days kept plastids after food removal, whereas earlier removal led to plastid breakdown. Stable retention develops during early feeding.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Figure 1; lines 143-173
evidence.note: Laboratory feeding duration affected plastid stability.

relations.note: Source explicitly identifies a sea slug.

concepts.label: Ferrar Glacier
concepts.learning_takeaway: A named glacier connects inland snow accumulation with an ice-flow route toward the sea.
concepts.card: Ferrar Glacier carries ice from Taylor Dome toward Antarctica's Ross Sea. Snow accumulating at the dome compresses into ice, some of which flows through this glacier and the Royal Society Range. The named route connects inland accumulation with ice reaching the coast.

evidence.locator: Snow accumulation and ice route; lines 268-270
evidence.note: Taylor Dome accumulation supplies the named glacier's seaward route.

relations.note: NASA explicitly describes Ferrar as a river of ice.

concepts.label: Frost heave
concepts.learning_takeaway: Growing ice in soil can raise the ground and deform a road surface.
concepts.card: Frost heave raises ground as ice grows within freezing soil, sometimes deforming road surfaces. Growing ice layers can draw in additional water that freezes, enlarging the layer. The movement therefore need not result solely from expansion of water already occupying soil pores.

evidence.locator: Density of frozen water and cryosuction; lines 89-94
evidence.note: Ice growth and additional water can heave frozen ground.

relations.note: Soil-water and ice-growth premises support editorial soil-physics placement.

concepts.label: Gathering in sewing
concepts.learning_takeaway: Draw longer cloth into small folds so it fits a shorter attaching edge.
concepts.card: Gathering draws a longer length of fabric into small folds so it fits a shorter attaching edge. In a machine-sewn ruffle, long stitches provide threads that can be pulled and adjusted. Distributing the folds lets the ruffle fit its band.

evidence.locator: Gathering stitches and ruffle attachment; lines 317-336
evidence.note: Pulled gathering threads fit a ruffle to its band.

relations.note: Source explicitly gathers a ruffle in a sewing project.

concepts.label: Glass transition
concepts.learning_takeaway: Amorphous polymer segment motion changes across a temperature range, separately from crystalline melting.
concepts.card: In an amorphous polymer, the glass transition marks a temperature range where chain segments gain substantial mobility. The material changes from glassy behavior toward rubbery behavior. This differs from melting crystalline regions: segment movement and crystalline order describe different changes.

evidence.locator: Long-range segmental motion; Glass Transition vs. Melting; lines 25-26 and 51-56
evidence.note: Segmental mobility changes; crystalline melting is distinguished.

relations.note: Source explicitly explains a polymer transition.

concepts.label: GN-z11
concepts.learning_takeaway: Resolve host-galaxy light from a compact source to investigate an early galaxy's unusual brightness.
concepts.card: GN-z11 is a distant galaxy seen about 430 million years after the Big Bang. NASA's 2024 Webb report describes extended host-galaxy light and a compact central source. Its colors and gas signatures support a black-hole interpretation, illustrating how indirect observations investigate early galaxies.

evidence.locator: Host galaxy and compact source; lines 322-336
evidence.note: Dated report resolves host and compact source with black-hole evidence.

relations.note: NASA explicitly identifies GN-z11 and its host component as a galaxy.

concepts.label: Grainline in woven fabric
concepts.learning_takeaway: Thread direction, rather than a printed stripe, determines whether fabric is on grain.
concepts.card: Grainline in woven fabric follows its threads, whose lengthwise and crosswise directions should meet at right angles. A printed stripe can be off grain. Aligning pieces by the print alone may therefore produce difficulties when matching patterns or cutting straight pieces.

evidence.locator: Checking fabric grain and printing; lines 69-73
evidence.note: Thread grain differs from printed design alignment.

relations.note: Cutting-alignment premises support an editorial sewing facet.

concepts.label: Guard cell
concepts.learning_takeaway: Paired guard cells control an opening used for leaf gas exchange.
concepts.card: Guard cells occur in pairs around a stoma, an opening in a plant's surface. By opening that pore, they let gases pass between the surrounding air and deeper leaf cells. The cells and the opening are distinct structures.

evidence.locator: Dermal tissue; lines 224-226
evidence.note: Paired cells open stomata for gas exchange.

relations.note: Passage locates guard cells around stomata.

concepts.label: Halocline
concepts.learning_takeaway: A salinity gradient can separate fresher surface water from saltier deep water.
concepts.card: A halocline is a layer where salinity changes rapidly with depth. Fresher surface water over saltier water can create one. It describes a salt gradient, while a pycnocline describes density and a thermocline describes temperature; these layers need not coincide.

evidence.locator: Main pycnocline and salinity layers; PDF page 2 (zero-based 1), lines 145-179
evidence.note: Ocean salinity-gradient layer distinguished from density and temperature layers.

relations.note: Source explicitly describes a salinity-stratified ocean zone.

concepts.label: Ham sandwich theorem
concepts.learning_takeaway: One plane can simultaneously bisect three three-dimensional volumes.
concepts.card: A single plane can simultaneously divide each of three finite-volume solids in three-dimensional space into equal volumes. The ham sandwich theorem extends this pattern: in n dimensions, one hyperplane can bisect n finite volumes, however differently they are positioned.

evidence.locator: Theorem statement and three-dimensional argument; lines 13-20
evidence.note: Simultaneous finite-volume bisection in matching dimension.

relations.note: Dimension and continuous-volume premises support editorial topology placement.

concepts.label: Hayabusa2
concepts.learning_takeaway: Returning physical asteroid samples lets laboratory analysis complement spacecraft observations.
concepts.card: The Japanese Hayabusa2 mission collected samples from asteroid Ryugu and returned them to Earth in 2020. Its instruments and small rovers explored the surface. Returning material lets laboratory analysis complement spacecraft observations, giving researchers physical asteroid samples to examine directly.

evidence.locator: Mission overview, sample return and craft design; lines 241, 264, 304-312
evidence.note: Ryugu exploration and completed 2020 sample return.

relations.note: Sampling and return support editorial space-exploration placement.
NASA explicitly names an asteroid as the mission's study target.

concepts.label: Immortal time bias
concepts.learning_takeaway: Survival needed to receive an exposure can create a misleading apparent treatment advantage.
concepts.card: In an observational treatment study, people classified as treated may need to survive from cohort entry until treatment begins. Misassigning that pre-treatment period to the treated group can create an apparent survival advantage unrelated to the treatment's effect.

evidence.locator: Immortal time bias; lines 204-206
evidence.note: Survival required before exposure assignment can produce spurious benefit.

relations.note: Source explicitly defines bias through cohort-entry and intervention timing.

concepts.label: Kleptoplasty
concepts.learning_takeaway: An animal can retain algal chloroplasts without retaining a complete algal cell.
concepts.card: Kleptoplasty is a symbiosis in which an animal retains chloroplasts taken from algal food. In Elysia chlorotica, these plastids remain in digestive cells and continue photosynthesis; the slug retains chloroplasts rather than complete algal cells.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Figure 1; lines 143-173
evidence.note: Retained food plastids continue photosynthesis.

relations.note: Introduction explicitly identifies plastid symbiosis.

concepts.label: LAGEOS
concepts.learning_takeaway: Passive reflecting satellites provide long-lived laser targets for measuring Earth's motion and shape.
concepts.card: LAGEOS is a pair of passive satellites covered with reflecting prisms. Laser measurements to these orbiting targets help investigate Earth's motion and shape, including plate movement and rotation. The satellites carry no electronics or sensors: their role is to provide stable reflective targets.

evidence.locator: LAGEOS 1 & 2 overview; lines 235-258
evidence.note: Passive reflecting satellite pair supports laser geodesy.

relations.note: NASA explicitly identifies a pair of orbiting satellites.

concepts.label: Leaf area index
concepts.learning_takeaway: Normalize leaf surface by ground area to describe canopy structure and model vegetation processes.
concepts.card: Leaf area index compares green leaf surface with ground area. For broadleaf plants it uses one leaf side; for conifers it uses half the total needle surface. This canopy measure helps model photosynthesis and exchanges of water, energy and carbon.

evidence.locator: Leaf Area Index definition and uses; lines 50-54
evidence.note: Leaf-surface ratio and plant-process modeling uses are explicit.

relations.note: Canopy and plant-process premises support editorial plant-physiology placement.

concepts.label: Length-time bias in cancer screening
concepts.learning_takeaway: Screening preferentially detects slower-growing cancers with longer preclinical windows.
concepts.card: Cancer screening disproportionately detects slower-growing cancers because they remain detectable before symptoms for longer. This length-time bias changes the mix of cancers found. More early-stage diagnoses can therefore occur without establishing that screening reduces deaths; detection patterns alone do not show the benefit.

evidence.locator: Length bias and overdiagnosis; lines 34-38
evidence.note: Longer preclinical windows enrich slower cancers and distort benefit measures.

relations.note: Source explicitly explains the bias in cancer screening.

concepts.label: Muon tomography
concepts.learning_takeaway: Natural muon scattering can reveal dense hidden structures without an added artificial radiation source.
concepts.card: Muon tomography uses scattering of naturally occurring cosmic-ray muons to reconstruct three-dimensional images of hidden material. Tracking changes in particle paths provides the information without adding an artificial radiation dose. Long exposures, limited position resolution and complex reconstruction remain practical challenges.

evidence.locator: Abstract; lines 15-17
evidence.note: Coulomb scattering enables natural-flux imaging with stated limitations.

relations.note: Source explicitly uses muon paths and scattering for imaging.

concepts.label: Nafion
concepts.learning_takeaway: A named fluorinated polymer membrane family conducts cations in electrochemical cells.
concepts.card: Nafion is a named family of fluorinated polymer membranes used in electrochemical applications. Its sulfonic membranes are based on a perfluorosulfonic-acid and PTFE copolymer and conduct positively charged ions. The membrane's polymer composition is tied to its role inside electrochemical cells.

evidence.locator: Membranes for a Wide Variety of Electrochemical Applications; lines 151-153; grades tables
evidence.note: Manufacturer identifies copolymer basis and cation conduction.

relations.note: Manufacturer explicitly identifies a polymer membrane family.

concepts.label: Negative pressure wound therapy
concepts.learning_takeaway: Controlled suction removes wound fluid while a sealed dressing supports healing.
concepts.card: Negative pressure wound therapy uses a sealed dressing connected to a suction pump. Removing wound fluid and reducing swelling can support healing. Clinicians select suitable wounds for this treatment; the intended outcome does not make the device appropriate for every wound.

evidence.locator: Definition and mechanism; lines 50-76; indications and contraindications, lines 78-104
evidence.note: Sealed-dressing suction removes fluid and reduces swelling.

relations.note: Provider-directed treatment supports editorial placement under medicine.
Source identifies wound healing as the intended outcome.

concepts.label: NIST SRM 610
concepts.learning_takeaway: Characterized trace-element glass can calibrate elemental measurements on Mars.
concepts.card: NIST SRM 610 is a trace-element glass reference material. A piece aboard NASA's Perseverance rover helps calibrate PIXL, an instrument that measures elements in Martian rocks. A characterized Earth material supplies a reference for interpreting measurements made on another planet.

evidence.locator: PIXL calibration discussion; lines 126-130
evidence.note: Glass reference material calibrates Perseverance's PIXL.

relations.note: Calibration premises support an editorial metrology application.
Source explicitly identifies SRM 610 as glass.

concepts.label: Nixtamalization
concepts.learning_takeaway: Alkaline maize processing changes dough preparation and nutrient availability.
concepts.card: Nixtamalization cooks and steeps maize in an alkaline solution, commonly made with lime. After washing, the kernels can be milled into dough for foods such as tortillas. Processing also increases calcium and makes niacin more available, connecting food preparation with chemical changes.

evidence.locator: What is nixtamalization? and nutritional changes; lines 27-41
evidence.note: Alkaline maize processing makes dough and changes nutrient availability.

relations.note: Cooking, soaking and milling support editorial food-processing placement.
Source explicitly names maize as the processed material.

concepts.label: Nonunion
concepts.learning_takeaway: A fracture that fails to heal differs from one that is merely healing slowly.
concepts.card: A nonunion is a broken bone that fails to heal, rather than a fracture that is merely healing slowly. Bone repair depends on stability, blood supply and nutrition. The distinction requires clinical and imaging context; it is not defined by one universal waiting period.

evidence.locator: Definition and bone healing; lines 118-123; diagnosis; lines 174-178
evidence.note: Failure differs from delay; stability and blood supply support healing.

relations.note: Source explicitly defines failure of a fracture to heal.

concepts.label: Occultation for weed control
concepts.learning_takeaway: Opaque covers block light while moisture and warmth exhaust newly sprouted weeds.
concepts.card: Occultation for weed control uses an opaque cover to block light over a garden bed. Warmth and moisture can encourage seeds to sprout, while darkness prevents the seedlings from sustaining growth. Weather and site conditions affect how the process performs.

evidence.locator: Clear versus opaque coverings; Quick facts and methods; lines 244-270, 287-299
evidence.note: Opaque covers combine germination conditions with light exclusion.

relations.note: Guide explicitly uses occultation for garden-bed weed control.

concepts.label: Photobleaching
concepts.learning_takeaway: Repeated illumination can irreversibly remove a molecule's fluorescence.
concepts.card: Photobleaching irreversibly removes a fluorescent molecule's ability to emit light through photochemical destruction during illumination. A fading image can therefore reflect damage to the fluorescent label rather than disappearance of the structure being observed. Not every loss of fluorescence is photobleaching.

evidence.locator: Fading, Quenching, and Photobleaching; lines 88-95
evidence.note: Irreversible fluorophore destruction is distinguished from broader fading.

relations.note: Source explains a mechanism of fluorescence loss.

concepts.label: Physical aging of polymers
concepts.learning_takeaway: Structural recovery changes a polymer's viscoelastic properties over time.
concepts.card: A polymer's properties can change through structural recovery, a process called physical aging. This affects viscoelastic behavior and engineering properties. Understanding a polymer glass therefore involves more than locating its glass transition: its recovering structure also matters.

evidence.locator: Abstract; lines 125-127
evidence.note: Structural recovery affects polymer mechanical properties.

relations.note: Abstract explicitly associates physical aging with polymer properties.

concepts.label: Pycnocline
concepts.learning_takeaway: A steep increase of density with depth can limit mixing between ocean layers.
concepts.card: A pycnocline is an ocean layer where density increases rapidly with depth. This stable density gradient can restrict exchange between surface and deeper water. Temperature, salinity or both may contribute, so a density boundary need not match one single temperature or salt boundary.

evidence.locator: Main pycnocline and salinity layers; PDF page 2 (zero-based 1), lines 145-179
evidence.note: Strong density gradient separates ocean layers and limits mixing.

relations.note: Source explicitly identifies a density-stratified ocean zone.

concepts.label: Refeeding syndrome
concepts.learning_takeaway: Restarting nutrition after malnutrition can produce dangerous electrolyte shifts.
concepts.card: After malnutrition, restarting nutrition can trigger dangerous electrolyte shifts as carbohydrate metabolism resumes. Cells draw phosphorus, potassium and magnesium from the blood, potentially leaving blood levels too low. Refeeding syndrome shows why nutritional recovery can require clinical monitoring as well as renewed food intake.

evidence.locator: Definition and electrolyte mechanism; lines 53, 69-79; clinical monitoring, lines 150-159
evidence.note: Renewed metabolism shifts electrolytes into cells after malnutrition.

relations.note: Source explicitly describes a complication following malnutrition.

concepts.label: Root hair
concepts.learning_takeaway: A fine epidermal-cell outgrowth provides an entry route for water and nutrients.
concepts.card: A root hair is a slender extension of a root epidermal cell, with its wall and membrane projecting into the surrounding growing medium. Water and nutrients enter through these fine outgrowths, connecting the root's surface to its supply.

evidence.locator: Dermal tissue; lines 224-226
evidence.note: Root epidermal outgrowths absorb water and nutrients.

relations.note: Passage identifies hairs in root dermal tissue.

concepts.label: Seam allowance
concepts.learning_takeaway: The fabric area between stitching and the raw edge is a separately planned construction allowance.
concepts.card: Seam allowance is the fabric area between a stitching line and the raw edge. A seam thus has distinct boundaries: where the pieces are joined and where they were cut. The intervening fabric belongs to the construction allowance, not the stitched line itself.

evidence.locator: Seam Allowance; PDF page 10 (zero-based 9), lines 224-226
evidence.note: Glossary defines area between stitching and raw edge.

relations.note: Sewing glossary explicitly defines the construction allowance.

concepts.label: Selvage
concepts.learning_takeaway: A firmly woven fabric edge can behave differently from the cloth body in a seam.
concepts.card: A selvage is the firmly woven edge running lengthwise along woven fabric. It can shrink more than the cloth's main area and pucker a seam, so its construction behavior deserves separate attention.

evidence.locator: Wearing versus design ease; fabric edges; lines 84, 154, 178
evidence.note: Firm lengthwise edges may shrink and pucker seams.

relations.note: Woven-edge premises support editorial placement under cloth.

concepts.label: Sentinel lymph node biopsy
concepts.learning_takeaway: Sampling the first draining lymph node helps investigate whether cancer has spread.
concepts.card: Sentinel lymph node biopsy identifies and samples the first node or nodes most likely to receive cancer spreading from a tumor. Examining them helps stage the cancer. A negative result suggests no spread to nearby nodes, but cannot guarantee it.

evidence.locator: Definition and procedure; lines 27-40; staging benefit, line 47; false-negative risk, line 59
evidence.note: Selected first nodes are removed and examined for cancer spread.

relations.note: Source explicitly describes a biopsy of selected lymph nodes.

concepts.label: Soil solarization
concepts.learning_takeaway: Clear plastic traps solar heat to suppress weeds and some soil pests.
concepts.card: Soil solarization covers soil with clear plastic to trap solar heat, suppressing weeds and some soil pests. Its effectiveness depends on sunlight, moisture and local conditions. The clear cover's heating mechanism differs from the light exclusion used by opaque covers.

evidence.locator: Clear versus opaque coverings; Quick facts and methods; lines 244-270, 287-299
evidence.note: Clear covers trap heat; results depend on conditions.

relations.note: Guide explicitly uses solarization to prepare garden beds.

concepts.label: Sperner's lemma
concepts.learning_takeaway: Boundary-constrained vertex colors guarantee a fully labeled small triangle.
concepts.card: Give a triangle's corners three different labels, and label every vertex of a triangulation with one of those three. Restrict boundary labels to each side's endpoint labels. Sperner's lemma guarantees a small triangle with all three labels.

evidence.locator: Opening statement and distinction; lines 13-18
evidence.note: Boundary labeling forces a fully labeled triangle.

relations.note: Triangulation and fixed-point premises support editorial topology placement.

concepts.label: Sperner's theorem
concepts.learning_takeaway: An inclusion-free family of subsets cannot exceed the middle binomial coefficient.
concepts.card: Choose subsets of an n-element set so none contains another. Their number cannot exceed the binomial coefficient for the middle layer of subsets. Selecting all subsets of a middle size attains the bound: inclusion restrictions impose a precise maximum.

evidence.locator: Theorem statement; lines 13-21
evidence.note: Antichain maximum is the middle binomial coefficient.

relations.note: Source identifies an extremal set-theory result.

concepts.label: Spinodal decomposition
concepts.learning_takeaway: Small composition fluctuations can grow without the nucleation barrier of a metastable mixture.
concepts.card: Spinodal decomposition separates an unstable mixture into phases as small composition fluctuations grow. Unlike nucleation in a metastable mixture, this process does not need to overcome a nucleation barrier. Whether fluctuations grow depends on the mixture's thermodynamic state.

evidence.locator: Opening explanatory paragraphs; lines 0-5
evidence.note: Barrierless separation contrasts with metastable nucleation.

relations.note: Phase-separation premises support editorial phase-transition placement.

concepts.label: Stale seedbed
concepts.learning_takeaway: Germinate and remove shallow weeds before sowing the crop, while avoiding fresh seed exposure.
concepts.card: A stale seedbed lets shallow weed seeds germinate before the crop is planted, then removes the seedlings. Limiting subsequent soil disturbance helps avoid exposing deeper seeds. The strategy uses the weeds' timing to reduce competition before crop growth begins.

evidence.locator: Precisely how does the stale seedbed work?; lines 57-62
evidence.note: Germination precedes crop planting; limited disturbance avoids new seed exposure.

relations.note: Source explicitly uses this method in vegetable crop production.

concepts.label: Stokes drift
concepts.learning_takeaway: Water parcels under a surface wave can drift even when their paths look nearly circular.
concepts.card: Beneath a progressive surface gravity wave, a water parcel can follow a nearly looping path that does not close, leaving net motion in the wave's direction. This Stokes drift differs from averaging velocity at a fixed point: following the parcel reveals transport.

evidence.locator: Overview and gravity-wave parcel trajectories; PDF pages 2 and 18-19; lines 26-31, 756-812
evidence.note: Open parcel trajectories distinguish Lagrangian drift from fixed-position averages.

relations.note: Surface-wave transport premises support editorial oceanography placement.

concepts.label: Surface plasmon resonance microscopy
concepts.learning_takeaway: Interfacial refractive-index changes support label-free optical measurements.
concepts.card: Surface plasmon resonance microscopy produces label-free images from refractive-index changes at an interface. Reflected light is collected through a microscope objective. Quantitative interpretation requires calibration and corrections for the optics, connecting an image's response to refractive-index values rather than appearance alone.

evidence.locator: Abstract; lines 125-128
evidence.note: Abstract describes imaging, optical corrections and calibration.

relations.note: Authors explicitly implement SPR imaging on a microscope.

concepts.label: Surgical anastomosis
concepts.learning_takeaway: Joining healthy tube ends can restore flow after removal or route around a blockage.
concepts.card: Surgical anastomosis joins tubular structures, such as blood vessels or sections of intestine, to restore flow. It can reconnect healthy ends after damaged tissue is removed or create a bypass. Transplant operations may also require these connections.

evidence.locator: What Is an Anastomosis?; surgical uses; lines 27, 55-82
evidence.note: Surgical tube connections restore flow or create bypasses.

relations.note: Surgical-procedure premises support editorial placement under medicine.
Source explicitly names transplantation as a use setting.

concepts.label: Symplast
concepts.learning_takeaway: Connected cytosols allow movement through cells joined by plasmodesmata.
concepts.card: The symplast comprises plant-cell cytoplasm connected through plasmodesmata, small links between neighboring cells. Water using this route moves within cells rather than along their walls. The distinction separates an internal transport compartment from the extracellular apoplast.

evidence.locator: The significance of the casparian strip; lines 234-242
evidence.note: Cytoplasmic connections define the internal route.

relations.note: Transport premises support editorial plant-physiology placement.

concepts.label: Thue–Morse sequence
concepts.learning_takeaway: Parity of binary digit sums generates a sequence by repeated complementary substitution.
concepts.card: Starting at index zero, the Thue–Morse sequence records whether each integer's binary digit sum is even or odd. Its zero-starting version begins 01101001. The same pattern grows by repeatedly replacing 0 with 01 and 1 with 10.

evidence.locator: Opening definition; substitution rules; lines 15-20 and 33-45
evidence.note: Binary digit parity and complementary substitution.

relations.note: Source explicitly identifies a number sequence.

concepts.label: van der Waerden's theorem
concepts.learning_takeaway: Finite colorings of the positive integers force arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions.
concepts.card: Color every positive integer using finitely many colors. Van der Waerden's theorem says that, for any chosen finite length, some arithmetic progression has that many terms all in one color. Regular spacing must emerge somewhere despite the coloring's freedom.

evidence.locator: Four equivalent formulations; lines 13-19
evidence.note: Finite colorings force monochromatic arithmetic progressions.

relations.note: Finite-color combinatorial existence supports editorial combinatorics placement.

concepts.label: Vaucheria litorea
concepts.learning_takeaway: This algal prey supplies the chloroplasts retained by Elysia chlorotica.
concepts.card: Vaucheria litorea is the alga eaten by Elysia chlorotica in its plastid partnership. Its chloroplasts enter the slug's digestive cells, while other algal organelles are not retained. The food organism supplies photosynthetic machinery without becoming a whole-cell resident.

evidence.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Figure 1; lines 143-173
evidence.note: Algal food supplies only the retained plastids.

relations.note: Introduction explicitly identifies algal food.

concepts.label: Wearing ease
concepts.learning_takeaway: Comfort room built into a pattern differs from extra room chosen for style.
concepts.card: Wearing ease is room beyond body measurements that a garment pattern includes for comfortable wear. Extra fullness chosen to change the garment's style is separately called design ease, serving a different purpose.

evidence.locator: Wearing versus design ease; fabric edges; lines 84, 154, 178
evidence.note: Comfort allowance differs from additional style fullness.

relations.note: Guide explicitly defines a sewing-pattern component.
